role_vocabulary.canvas: Page/figure background. White in 272/272 architecture figures -- never tint it.
role_vocabulary.container: Fill of an outer group or region box (a host, a plane, a subsystem).
role_vocabulary.lane: Fill of a swimlane / horizontal or vertical band (a phase, a tier, a timeline row).
role_vocabulary.module: Default component-box fill: the colour most boxes get.
role_vocabulary.module-alt: Second and third component fills, for a different *kind* of component.
role_vocabulary.accent: Fill that marks the novel component or the main path. At most 1-2 per figure.
role_vocabulary.stroke: Box outlines. Near-neutral and dark; 0.5-1pt in the corpus.
role_vocabulary.text: Primary label text. Near-black; never lighter than the module it sits on.
role_vocabulary.text-muted: Secondary text: annotations, units, greyed-out labels.
role_vocabulary.arrow: Default connector colour, usually the same neutral as `stroke`.
role_vocabulary.arrow-accent: Highlighted connector: the request path, the error, the new flow.
role_vocabulary.legend: Legend box background, when the legend sits inside the figure.

general_rules.canvas: #ffffff - 272/272 architecture figures use a white page background.

distinct_fills_per_figure.note: median 5 distinct hexes overall (fills + strokes + text)

saturated_fills_per_figure.note: chroma >= 0.40; 106/272 figures use none and 86 use exactly one - treat 2 as the ceiling

grey.note: grey marks existing/unchanged components; 113/272 encoding.color_means strings mention grey

accent.note: one accent per figure is the norm; a second one only for the highlighted connector

text.note: near-black by default; 45 of 103 recorded text/module pairs fall below 4.5:1 - do not copy that

ground.note: How the outer group boxes are filled in the good architecture figures with semantic records: outline-containers = nesting >= 2 but no container/lane fill (bare outlines, often dashed); flat-on-canvas = no containers at all; the rest by the container fill. Grey grounds are a minority.

palettes.name: Blue modules, orange accent
palettes.description: Light-blue component boxes on a light-grey ground, with one orange box or arrow for the contribution; cream and pale-green as second and third fills.
palettes.when_to_use: The default choice for a whole-system overview. Safest when the figure has one obvious novel component and 6-15 boxes.
palettes.contrast_notes: every role pair clears 4.5:1 with the listed text colour

palettes.name: Green modules, red highlight
palettes.description: Pale-green component boxes with a mid-grey container; red is reserved for the highlighted path, the error case or the outlined contribution.
palettes.when_to_use: Pipelines and layered stacks where one path (a failure, a fast path, the paper's addition) has to jump out of an otherwise calm figure.
palettes.contrast_notes: text on accent is 4.4:1 (#191919 on #ff0000) - use #ffffff for labels inside that box

palettes.name: High-contrast primaries
palettes.description: Near-white boxes with heavy near-black outlines, a mid-grey container, and fully saturated primaries (deep red, pure blue, orange) for the few elements that matter.
palettes.when_to_use: Small single-column figures and TikZ figures that will be printed small: maximum legibility, colour used sparingly and loudly.
palettes.contrast_notes: text on accent is 2.7:1 (#191919 on #c00000) - use #ffffff for labels inside that box

palettes.name: Cream and pastel mix
palettes.description: Cream default boxes with pale blue, green and pink alternates, dashed grey containers, and a saturated orange only where emphasis is needed.
palettes.when_to_use: Dense figures with many small boxes of several kinds (encoder blocks, queues, caches) where every box needs a fill but none may shout.
palettes.contrast_notes: container: corpus value #fce5cd replaced by #d9d9d9 (cluster-modal light neutral, kept >=0.08 lightness away from the module fill); accent: corpus value #ffe699 replaced by #ffc000 (cluster-modal accent that separates from the module fill)

palettes.name: Grey scaffold with pastel tints
palettes.description: Grey is the default box and the container; cream, pale blue and pale pink mark the few boxes that differ, with orange for the accent.
palettes.when_to_use: Figures that reuse an existing system: grey for what already exists, a tint only where the paper adds or changes something.
palettes.contrast_notes: container: corpus value #e7e6e6 replaced by #f2f2f2 (cluster-modal light neutral, kept >=0.08 lightness away from the module fill); lane: corpus value #d9d9d9 replaced by #fff2cc (cluster-modal light fill distinct from the container)

palettes.name: Greyscale only
palettes.description: No hue at all: near-white boxes, a mid-grey container band, black outlines and arrows; emphasis comes from weight and dashed outlines.
palettes.when_to_use: Print-first venues, figures that must survive a black-and-white print-out, and figures whose message is structure rather than kind.
palettes.contrast_notes: container: corpus value #f2f2f2 replaced by #d9d9d9 (cluster-modal light neutral, kept >=0.08 lightness away from the module fill); lane: corpus value #f2f2f2 replaced by #ebebeb (cluster-modal light fill distinct from the container); accent: corpus value #ff0000 replaced by #666666 (monochrome family: darkest grey its members use for emphasis (borrow #c00000 only for a highlighted path)); text on accent is 3.7:1 (#000000 on #666666) - use #ffffff for labels inside that box

palettes.name: Blue monochrome
palettes.description: One blue family end to end -- pale blue fills, a mid blue for the second tier and a strong Office blue for the accent and arrows.
palettes.when_to_use: Hardware and micro-architecture figures, and any figure where colour should carry depth (light = outer, dark = inner) rather than category.
palettes.contrast_notes: lane: corpus value #deebf7 replaced by #d9d9d9 (cluster-modal light fill distinct from the container); text on accent is 2.7:1 (#333333 on #4472c4) - use #ffffff for labels inside that box

palettes.name: Warm container bands
palettes.description: Cream, peach and pale-green bands name the phases or planes; the boxes inside stay pale, and a gold accent marks the key step.
palettes.when_to_use: Layered or two-plane figures where the *regions* are the message (control plane vs data plane, offline vs online, per-section bands).
palettes.contrast_notes: every role pair clears 4.5:1 with the listed text colour

palettes.name: Multi-hue categorical
palettes.description: Four to six distinct hues (green, pink, cream, blue) used as categories rather than as decoration, a deep crimson accent, and saturated chips from extra_fills for the legend swatches.
palettes.when_to_use: Figures where colour *is* the data: colour-coded flows, per-tenant resources, heterogeneous engines. Always ship a legend with it.
palettes.contrast_notes: text on accent is 2.2:1 (#231f20 on #b1001c) - use #ffffff for labels inside that box

palettes.name: Amber highlight on neutral
palettes.description: Neutral grey lanes and peach/white boxes, with a dark gold-amber fill reserved for the one component or step the paper contributes.
palettes.when_to_use: Before/after and baseline-vs-ours figures: keep everything neutral and let a single amber block carry the claim.
palettes.contrast_notes: container: corpus value #fff2cc replaced by #d9d9d9 (cluster-modal light neutral, kept >=0.08 lightness away from the module fill)

palettes.name: Cool grey and cyan
palettes.description: Cool light-grey containers with pale cyan-blue boxes and a warm tan counterpart, near-black outlines and a deep teal accent.
palettes.when_to_use: Orchestration and control-plane figures that need a quieter, cooler look than blue-orange while still being in colour.
palettes.contrast_notes: lane: corpus value #f2f2f2 replaced by #e7e7e7 (cluster-modal light fill distinct from the container); text on accent is 2.9:1 (#262626 on #117788) - use #ffffff for labels inside that box

palettes.name: Blue boxes, outline containers
palettes.description: Light-blue component boxes straight on the white page; groups and hosts are drawn as outlines only (0.5-0.75 pt, solid or dashed, no fill), with a strong Office blue or an orange box for the contribution.
palettes.when_to_use: The transparent-ground twin of blue-orange / blue-mono: the same blue vocabulary when the figure has several nested groups and a grey slab behind each would stack up muddy; the outline keeps nesting legible.
palettes.contrast_notes: text on accent is 4.1:1 (#0d0d0d on #4472c4) - use #ffffff for labels inside that box

palettes.name: Near-white boxes, ink outlines, one accent
palettes.description: White or near-white boxes with black 0.75-1 pt outlines, thin outline containers (often rounded or dashed) and at most one saturated fill - crimson, orange or blue - on the box the paper adds.
palettes.when_to_use: Small single-column figures and TikZ-like drawings printed small: the transparent twin of high-contrast. Everything reads in greyscale, colour is spent on one element.
palettes.contrast_notes: text on accent is 2.9:1 (#010000 on #b1001c) - use #ffffff for labels inside that box

palettes.name: Cream and pastel boxes, outline containers
palettes.description: Cream / peach default boxes with pale-blue, pale-green and pink alternates for the other kinds of component, an amber or red accent, and containers drawn as bare outlines on white.
palettes.when_to_use: Dense figures with several kinds of boxes (the cream-pastel look) when the regions should not add yet another fill; the pastel fills already separate the kinds, the outline only delimits the region.
palettes.contrast_notes: every role pair clears 4.5:1 with the listed text colour

palettes.name: Each region its own pastel tint
palettes.description: Two to four regions (planes, hosts, phases) each filled with a different very light tint - cream, pale green, pale blue, pink - with white or pale-blue boxes inside and a dark-gold or red accent. `container`, `lane` and `legend` list the first three tints; `region_tints` has the full set.
palettes.when_to_use: Figures whose message is the split into regions (client / server, control / data plane, before / after) when a legend for the regions should be avoided: the tint names the region.
palettes.contrast_notes: every role pair clears 4.5:1 with the listed text colour

palettes.name: Green boxes, outline containers
palettes.description: Pale-green component boxes with pale-blue / pink alternates, red reserved for the highlighted path, containers as solid or dashed outlines on white.
palettes.when_to_use: Pipelines and stacks where one path must jump out (the green-red look) drawn without a grey ground, typically with dashed host or trust boundaries.
palettes.contrast_notes: text on accent is 3.5:1 (#2c2c2c on #ff0000) - use #ffffff for labels inside that box

palettes.name: Pale-blue ground, warm boxes
palettes.description: A pale-blue container behind cream / orange component boxes (or pale-blue lanes behind white boxes), dark outlines, a crimson or Office-blue accent.
palettes.when_to_use: One dominant region (a host, a chip, a runtime) that should read as a unit; the warm boxes pop against the cool ground without any saturated fill.
palettes.contrast_notes: text on accent is 3.0:1 (#0d0d0d on #c00000) - use #ffffff for labels inside that box

palettes.name: Greyscale, outline containers
palettes.description: No hue at all: light-grey or white boxes, black outlines and text, containers as black or dashed outlines on the white page; red or blue is used at most for a word or an arrow.
palettes.when_to_use: B/W-safe figures and print-first venues when the structure is nested: the transparent twin of greyscale, where a mid-grey container slab would swallow the grey boxes.
palettes.contrast_notes: every role pair clears 4.5:1 with the listed text colour

palettes.name: Cream ground, blue boxes
palettes.description: A cream or peach container behind pale-blue component boxes, pale-green alternates and an amber accent; warm-bands is the banded version of the same look.
palettes.when_to_use: Warm, print-friendly figures with one main region; the cool boxes separate cleanly from the warm ground, and the amber accent stays in the same temperature.
palettes.contrast_notes: every role pair clears 4.5:1 with the listed text colour

palettes.name: Categorical hues, outline containers
palettes.description: Four to six distinct hues used as categories (pink, blue, peach, green, lavender boxes), a crimson or magenta accent, and containers or panel frames drawn as outlines on white.
palettes.when_to_use: Colour is the data (traffic classes, tenants, engine kinds) and the figure also has regions: the transparent twin of multi-hue-categorical, so the categorical fills stay the only colour on the page.
palettes.contrast_notes: corpus value #598980 is tinted (chroma 0.19); replaced by the neutral #404040; text on accent is 2.1:1 (#231f20 on #a50040) - use #ffffff for labels inside that box

palettes.name: Pale-green ground, blue boxes
palettes.description: A pale-green container or band behind pale-blue boxes with cream alternates and an orange accent.
palettes.when_to_use: A quieter alternative to the blue ground when blue is already taken by the boxes; common for the trusted / secure region (green = trusted) of a two-region figure.
palettes.contrast_notes: corpus value #4e5c3e is tinted (chroma 0.12); replaced by the neutral #1a1a1a; corpus value #385723 is tinted (chroma 0.20); replaced by the neutral #404040

palettes.name: Charon: ink outlines, identity pastels, grey headers
palettes.description: The palette of the named style 'charon' (references/styles/charon.md), measured from the seven diagrams of the Charon paper (MLSys 2026). Every box has a dark-ink outline; four pastels each name one component or concept and keep that meaning across all figures of the paper (blue, peach, mint, pink); grey marks structure (title bars, platform cards, bookend bars); there is no accent fill -- 'ours' versus 'the old way' is said in green and red text.
palettes.when_to_use: Only with meta.style = 'charon' (or when the user asks for this look). Suits figures whose components fall into 3-4 kinds that recur across several figures of one paper.
palettes.origin: style-reference: hand-measured from assets/exemplars/styles/charon/ (not a corpus cluster; palette_cluster.py does not produce it -- re-add by hand if palettes.json is regenerated)

identity_fills.name: blue
identity_fills.in_charon: graph operators, profiling engine, transformer blocks, forward

identity_fills.name: peach
identity_fills.in_charon: prediction engine, value generation, outputs, torch steps

identity_fills.name: mint
identity_fills.in_charon: analytical engine, norm layers, communication, expected output

identity_fills.name: pink
identity_fills.in_charon: graph simulation, key generation, backward, pruning tool

identity_fills.name: grey
identity_fills.in_charon: title bars, platform card, fused engine, embedding / LM head, bookend bars

state_pairs.note: mechanism figures: one hue per resource or owner, solid = normal / full, pale + dotted outline = degraded / not resident

palettes.contrast_notes: black text on every fill clears 7:1; white text only on #178d6a and #3f90de

mechanism.note: Mechanism figures (kind 2) use the same 21 families: each of the 154 good mechanism figures with a semantic record was matched to the family nearest to its module / accent / container / lane / alt hexes (CIELAB, roles compared pairwise, 20 for a filled ground against a transparent one): 42% sit within 15 and 81% within 25 of a family, and a clustering of the mechanism records on their own (palette_cluster.py --subtype mechanism, k=8) reproduces existing families rather than new ones. What differs is the ground -- most mechanism figures have no container fill at all -- and the STATE colours: a mechanism figure spends colour on what changed, what is wrong, what is current and what is old, not on component kinds. Frequencies, not rules: figures of this kind vary a great deal, so treat the table as the corpus habit to start from.

wrong / failed / removed.note: red family in 11 of 19 uses; a crossed-out or struck element often adds a grey ghost

old / inactive / ghost / before.note: grey in 22 of 35 uses; dashed outline when the element is gone rather than idle

current / active / selected / this step.note: yellow / amber, blue or red about equally (30 records); pick the one the palette does not already use for a component kind

correct / new / added / ours.note: green when paired with a red wrong case, otherwise the accent of the palette; only 13 records name it

mechanism.source: lab/extracted/corpus_semantics.jsonl kind == mechanism (152 records, 2026-09-20); scripts/distill/palette_cluster.py --subtype mechanism, palette_grounds.py --subtype mechanism, and a keyword tally of style.palette[].used_for
